source: Wikipedia (accessed 2026-11) TRIZ
finding: Altshuller and colleagues began TRIZ in 1946 in a Soviet Navy inventions office. He was arrested in 1950 and freed after Stalin's death. First paper 1956. TRIZ was built by screening patents to see which contradiction each invention resolved and how.
numbers: Page says only 'hundreds of thousands of inventions'. It gives no patent count, no inventiveness-level percentages, no matrix size.
quote: the account of the matrix is 'actually the simplification of some fact'
limits: Encyclopedia source, not primary. Corporate claims (Intel 212.5M dollars ROI over 21 months; Samsung 100M dollars saved) carry 'citation needed' tags.
agent_relevance: The method is a patent-derived catalogue of reframes, not a tested theory of thought. Treat its claims as design heuristics (G7: must pay for itself).

source: Wikipedia (accessed 2026-11) Ideal final result
finding: Ideal final result (IFR) is stated as the ultimate solution where the desired result is achieved by itself, with no added system, cost or harm. The page gives no formula and no evidence.
numbers: none
quote: the ultimate solution of a problem when the desired result is achieved by itself
limits: Definition cited to a Polish TRIZ knowledge page. No test of IFR as a stand-alone technique was found.
agent_relevance: IFR is a goal-restating reframe (O4/O8 candidate): 'what if the function happened with no new part?' It is cheap to run as a typed prompt but has no measured effect alone.

source: Wikipedia (accessed 2026-11) Genrich Altshuller
finding: Biography only: born 1926, patent-office clerk, co-wrote Psychology of inventive creativity (1956) with Shapiro, jailed 1950-1954, founded an inventive-creativity institute in 1971, died 1998.
numbers: none on the method
limits: Page has no data on patents analysed, levels of inventiveness, or the matrix.
agent_relevance: Confirms that founding numbers (patent counts, 5 levels) could not be checked from open pages this session; do not cite them as verified.

source: Trapp and Warschat (2024) LLM-based Extraction of Contradictions from Patents (arXiv 2403.14258) - background section
finding: States the two insights Altshuller drew from manual patent analysis: resolving contradictions between system parameters often gives highly innovative solutions, and many high-grade innovations transfer an existing solution from another domain. Also says TRIZ rests on a historic patent set and ignores newer patents.
numbers: Cites 85-90 percent of world technical knowledge being in patents; over 20 million patents exist; average patent about 10,000 words.
quote: the resolution of contradictions between system parameters often creates highly innovative solutions
limits: Secondary statement by the authors, cited to TRIZ literature, not a measurement. The 85-90 percent figure is an old oft-repeated claim.
agent_relevance: Gives the two mechanisms to test in an agent: (1) name the trade-off, (2) borrow a solved pattern from a distant field. These map to O4 (reframe by contradiction) and analogy transfer.

source: Trapp and Warschat (2024) LLM-based Extraction of Contradictions from Patents - main experiment
finding: Zero-shot GPT-4 (gpt-4-1106-preview) was asked to find TRIZ contradictions in the state-of-the-art section of 100 patents that experts had annotated as containing one. It found at least one in all 100. Sentence-level F1 was 0.56, on par with the best fine-tuned PaTRIZ classifiers (weighted F1 0.54).
numbers: N=100 patents from PaGAN (3,200 patents, 1,600 with contradictions). Annotated sentences 3.81 per patent; GPT-4 got 2.69 right (recall 0.71), 3.19 false positives (precision 0.46), F1 0.56. BERTScore-F1 0.93 for extracted sentences, 0.88 for the generated summary.
limits: Only 2 patents analysed in detail. Arbitrary 100-patent sample. BERTScore measures text similarity, not logical correctness. Prompt carried the 39 parameter definitions.
agent_relevance: Models can spot trade-off statements about as well as trained classifiers, but over-detect (precision 0.46). A checker is needed before any contradiction is trusted (G2, G3).

source: Trapp and Warschat (2024) LLM-based Extraction of Contradictions from Patents - negative control
finding: On 100 patents annotated as having NO contradiction, GPT-4 still reported contradictions in 86 of 100. Mean 4.84 sentences extracted per patent.
numbers: 86 of 100 patents flagged; 87 contradictions found; 0.00 annotated sentences by definition, so all flagged sentences count as false positives against the annotation.
limits: The no-contradiction label is 'supposed to' hold (authors' wording); the annotation may miss implicit trade-offs. So some flags may be valid.
agent_relevance: A contradiction-finder that fires almost always is a signal-free trigger. It violates G1 (doubt only on a signal). Use it only after a failed check, not as a gate.

source: Trapp and Warschat (2024) - PaTRIZ baseline
finding: The earlier PaTRIZ pipeline (Guarino, Samet, Cavallucci 2022) used two BERT classifiers. Stage 1 got F1 0.37 and stage 2 got F1 0.65 on sentence classification. End-to-end, only one in three extracted contradictions matched an expert annotation.
numbers: Stage-1 F1 0.37 (2,276 positive sentences); stage-2 F1 0.65 (3,709 negative sentences); pair match about 0.33.
limits: Reported second-hand in Trapp and Warschat, not read in the original.
agent_relevance: Shows that automated contradiction mining was weak before LLMs and is still modest. Expect noisy typed reframes.

source: Chen et al. (2024) TRIZ-GPT: An LLM-augmented method for problem-solving (arXiv 2408.05897) - contradiction step
finding: GPT-4 was asked to find TRIZ improving/worsening parameter pairs in 34 textbook cases. Chain-of-thought gave the best recall; few-shot examples cut recall by more than half while raising precision a little.
numbers: GPT-4, collection A (34 test cases): recall/precision Basic 0.675/0.259, CoT 0.691/0.310, Few-shot 0.245/0.333, CoT+Few-shot 0.247/0.298.
limits: Recall is the main metric; precision is low (0.26-0.33). Authors say few-shot may teach the model the number of pairs. Textbook cases may be in training data. Gold labels are textbook analyses.
agent_relevance: Prompt wording changes TRIZ output counts a lot. An agent should have code, not the model, decide how many contradictions to carry (G5).

source: Chen et al. (2024) TRIZ-GPT - GPT-3.5 vs GPT-4 on post-cutoff cases
finding: On 10 cases published after April 2023, GPT-4 had higher recall than GPT-3.5 with basic and CoT prompts. With few-shot the order reversed. GPT-3.5 left out parameter numbers in 2 of 10 outputs.
numbers: Recall (GPT-3.5 vs GPT-4): Basic 0.400 vs 0.544; CoT 0.400 vs 0.544; Few-shot 0.304 vs 0.288; CoT+Few-shot 0.383 vs 0.275. Precision GPT-4 0.327-0.400. Cases average 5.5 pairs.
limits: N=10, no significance tests. Models output more pairs than the 5.5 gold average, which inflates recall.
agent_relevance: Model size helps only under some prompts. Gains are not robust. Supports G7: test each scaffold element against the plain model.

source: Chen et al. (2024) TRIZ-GPT - solution step
finding: Given a known principle, GPT-4 wrote solutions and was scored by embedding cosine similarity to the original published solution. Prompt strategy made no real difference.
numbers: N=84 cases, 3 solutions per principle. Mean cosine similarity 0.829 (SD 0.031) Basic, 0.823 CoT, 0.824 few-shot, 0.824 CoT+few-shot. Differences not significant.
limits: Cosine similarity to one reference solution is a weak proxy for quality or novelty. No human ratings. Principle-identification recall/precision not reported.
agent_relevance: Similarity to a known answer rewards recall of known solutions, not invention. G8: novelty must be judged by running or by a check, not similarity.

source: Jiang, Li, Qian, Zhang, Luo (2025) AutoTRIZ (arXiv 2403.13002 v2/v4) - consistency
finding: GPT-4 was run 100 times per problem to pick the contradiction. Output varied. Only 7 of 10 textbook cases matched or half-matched the textbook analysis inside the top 3 detections.
numbers: 10 cases from 7 textbooks; 100 runs each; Shannon entropy scale 0 to 6.64 (log2 100); 7/10 match or half-match in top 3; 4 cases (5-8) had a dominant top-1.
limits: Textbook analysis called not a gold standard by the authors. No human raters, no baseline LLM, no statistical tests. One model version (GPT-4 20231106).
agent_relevance: Contradiction choice is unstable across samples. Counting samples and taking the mode (code) is safer than one model pick. Samples are not independent (G4).

source: Jiang et al. (2025) AutoTRIZ - application case
finding: AutoTRIZ was used to design a battery thermal management system. The resulting FHP-BTMS scheme beat two existing schemes on modelled metrics. Check was one co-author expert, no outside rater, no plain-LLM baseline.
numbers: Volumetric energy density 206 vs 166 Wh/L (+24%); thermal efficiency eTMS 21.66 vs 13.18 (+64%, reported); grouping efficiency 43% vs 34% (reported +26%); 100 trials for contradiction frequency.
limits: Single case. No ablation showing TRIZ steps caused the gain. Authors admit hallucinations, no fact-check module, one contradiction per run, TRIZ base limited to 40 principles.
agent_relevance: Best case in the field is still an uncontrolled demonstration. It does not show TRIZ beats an LLM given the same domain prompt.

source: Jiang et al. (2025) AutoTRIZ - baseline claim
finding: No quantitative comparison with plain GPT-4 is reported. The only comparison is the remark that vanilla ChatGPT's TRIZ output 'always included apparent errors'.
numbers: No counts, no scores, no N.
limits: Anecdotal. The central claim of AutoTRIZ (LLM plus TRIZ beats LLM alone) is untested in this paper.
agent_relevance: Same gap as the whole literature: no matched-compute test of typed TRIZ reframes versus free reframing.

source: Szczepanik and Chudziak (2025) TRIZ Agents (arXiv 2506.18783)
finding: Eight GPT-4o agents (manager plus mechanical, electrical, control, safety, TRIZ, operations, documentation specialists) ran a six-step TRIZ workflow on one gantry-crane case published after the model cutoff. Judged qualitatively against the paper's solution.
numbers: 2 runs assessed; 60-80 graph node calls and 150,000-250,000 tokens per run; both physical contradictions matched; only 1 principle overlapped; 6 useful connections missed; one of two case solutions found (sliding mode control antiswing), circuit breaker missed.
limits: One case, one model, temperature 0.5, no baseline, no raters, no diversity metric. TRIZ specialist rarely used its RAG tool. No feedback loop.
agent_relevance: Multi-agent TRIZ costs 150-250k tokens for partial recovery of one solution. Conflicts with G9 (no debate) and G7 (pay for itself) unless shown against a single call.

source: Xu, Wu, Zhao (2026) TRIZ-RAGNER (arXiv 2602.23656)
finding: Retrieval-augmented GPT extracting improving and worsening TRIZ parameters from patent sentences beat sequence-labelling models and plain GPT. Ablation shows each of retrieval, reranking and structured prompt helps.
numbers: PaTRIZ about 3,000 instances, 8:1:1 split, 3 seeds. P/R/F1 (%): BiLSTM-CRF 62.4/59.1/60.7; BERT-CRF 69.8/67.3/68.5; RoBERTa-CRF 72.6/70.9/71.7; GPT zero-shot 75.1/72.4/73.7; GPT+prompt 78.3/75.6/76.9; TRIZ-RAGNER 85.6/82.9/84.2. Ablation F1: no retrieval 78.1, no rerank 79.8, no structured prompt 76.6.
limits: Dataset described as about 3,000 instances, which sits oddly beside other counts of PaTRIZ; model and retriever names are not given. Exact-match scoring. Preprint, not peer reviewed as far as I could see.
agent_relevance: Grounding the model in the 39-parameter table raises accuracy about 7 points over best prompt-only. Supports giving the agent the fixed TRIZ tables as tools, not memory.

source: TRIZBench (2026) ACL Findings 1798 - dataset
finding: Largest TRIZ benchmark found. Built from open TRIZ web material and US patents with human checks. Three tasks: contradiction prediction, inventive principle prediction, grounded reasoning.
numbers: 1,354 cases; 1,679 contradictions; 2,630 solutions; only 491 contradictions (29.2%) carry TRIZ parameters; 429 unique patents, 257 (56.2%) with parameters; case text average 278 tokens; 95% of a checked sample judged semantically valid by one annotator; small calibration study on 5 cases with 6 human raters.
limits: Labels come from published TRIZ cases, so they inherit the practitioners' subjectivity. Only 29% of contradictions have parameter labels.
agent_relevance: Gives a measurable testbed. Also shows that most published TRIZ cases lack the formal parameter labels the matrix needs.

source: TRIZBench (2026) - contradiction prediction (Table 2)
finding: Spotting that a contradiction exists is easy. Recovering the correct improving/worsening pair is hard. Few-shot gains are small and inconsistent. LoRA fine-tuning of an 8B model beat zero-shot frontier prompting.
numbers: Case-level detection F1 (HasF1) 0.75-0.87 for prompted models; pair F1 at threshold 0.65: Gemini-2.5-Pro 0.36 ZS and 0.42 FS, Qwen3-8B 0.31 FS, LLaMA3.1-70B 0.32 ZS. LoRA best detection F1 0.90. Patent Hit@3: prompted 0.13-0.24, PatentSBERTa retrieval 0.26, LoRA best 0.28.
limits: Semantic-match threshold 0.65 is a choice. Table rows partly garbled in extraction. Some cell values (LoRA rows) could not be assigned to models with certainty.
agent_relevance: Models name that a trade-off exists but mislabel which two things trade off. Reframes built on the wrong pair will misdirect S5 revisions.

source: TRIZBench (2026) - inventive principle prediction (Table 3)
finding: The classic contradiction matrix lookup beats direct LLM prompting at picking principles. TF-IDF text matching does even better. The best system uses the LLM only to rerank matrix candidates.
numbers: Hit@3 / Recall@3, cases then patents: Matrix 0.67/0.26 and 0.48/0.39; TF-IDF 0.69/0.35 and 0.56/0.42; Qwen3-8B ZS 0.39/0.12 and 0.27/0.18; Qwen3-8B FS 0.51/0.19 and 0.25/0.15; Gemini-2.5-Pro ZS 0.45/0.23 and 0.31/0.26; Gemini-2.5-Pro FS 0.52/0.21 and 0.35/0.27; Matrix-Rerank Qwen3-8B 0.71/0.29 and 0.59/0.47; LLaMA3.1-8B Matrix-Rerank 0.68/0.24 and 0.55/0.36.
quote: LLMs are most effective as selectors over matrix-consistent candidates
limits: Gold principles are the ones the case author chose, not proof they were the best. Hit@3 is lenient: random picks of 3 from 40 would hit a single gold principle about 7.5% of the time (my calculation).
agent_relevance: Strongest design signal: code produces the candidate set (matrix lookup), the model only picks among them. This is exactly G5 and the 'code selects' rule for any O4 typed reframe.

source: TRIZBench (2026) - grounded reasoning and calibration
finding: Solution-evidence grounding rises with the number of retrieved sentences and tracks principle accuracy. Authors say labeled-TRIZ accuracy alone can be misleading, since plausible principles are often not the source-associated ones.
numbers: PatentSBERTa best retriever for evidence alignment; improving 0.14 at F1 as stated in extracted text (exact table not read). Principle Hit@3 up to 0.71 on cases and 0.59 on patents.
limits: Figure 3 values not read. Evidence F1 is against retrieved, not human, evidence sets.
agent_relevance: A reframe should cite concrete text from the problem, as in G2. Citing sentences is checkable; naming a principle is not.

source: Lee et al. (2026) TRIZ-Inspired Text-to-CAD (arXiv 2606.21378)
finding: Claude Sonnet 4.5 wrote FreeCAD scripts for a chair. Adding a TRIZ contradiction (strength vs weight of moving object) and one principle cut mass while keeping stress low. A plain 'lighter' prompt cut more mass but doubled deflection.
limits: One chair, one run per design, one load case, no variance, no expert rating. Only the Segmentation variant held stress flat. Text says deformations stay below 0.5 mm but vanilla reached 0.574 mm. Preprint.
agent_relevance: A checked outcome (FEA) exists here. Only 1 of 4 TRIZ variants avoided a stress penalty, so principle choice matters and needs a test (G3), not trust.

source: Ogot and Okudan (2006) Integrating systematic creativity into first-year engineering design curriculum, Int. J. Eng. Educ. 22(1)
finding: Penn State first-year design course taught contradiction matrix and 40 principles in 2 sections. 16 TRIZ teams versus 24 teams from 3 randomly chosen non-TRIZ sections on the same fume-hood problem. TRIZ teams produced about twice as many feasible concepts.
numbers: TRIZ teams 8.94 feasible concepts per team vs 4.42; TRIZ sections averaged 35 unique solutions vs 16.3; 21 unique concepts found only by TRIZ teams vs 8 only by non-TRIZ; 64 TRIZ students vs 96 non-TRIZ.
limits: Quantity only, no novelty or quality. No random assignment to condition. Student complaints: too many tables, tedious lookup. Instructors had to keep teams on task. Authors' own enthusiasm may bias.
agent_relevance: Early positive result is on counts of ideas under instructor supervision. Not a test of idea quality.

source: Vargas-Hernandez, Schmidt, Okudan (2012) Experimental assessment of TRIZ effectiveness in idea generation, ASEE 2012-4512
finding: Controlled replication at three universities (UTEP, Maryland, Penn State). TRIZ raised novelty and variety but lowered quantity; several differences were not significant. Authors say some results are only a trend.
numbers: UTEP 21 control and 9 TRIZ seniors; Maryland 20 control and 21 TRIZ. Quantity p-values 0.2879, 0.5409, 0.6291 (not significant). Novelty p-values 0.0004, 0.0145, 0.5786 (two of three sites significant). Quantity means: control about 2-15, TRIZ about 1.7-16.3 (table garbled in extraction, so site mapping uncertain).
limits: Small samples, tables garbled by PDF, site-to-number mapping not confirmed. Different warm-ups at different sites. Shah et al. metrics from a genealogy tree.
agent_relevance: Fails to replicate the 2006 quantity gain. Net effect is fewer but more novel and varied ideas. Fits the schema: use TRIZ-type reframes to widen S3 variety, not to raise count.

source: Gero, Jiang, Williams (2012) Design cognition differences when using structured and unstructured concept generation creativity techniques, ICDC 2012
finding: Protocol analysis (FBS coding) of 11 two-student teams doing one brainstorming task and one TRIZ task. TRIZ sessions spent far more effort on problem aspects (goals, requirements); brainstorming sessions on solution aspects. The gap shrank by the second half.
numbers: 22 senior mechanical engineering students, 11 teams. Problem-solution issue index: brainstorming 0.192 (SD 0.049) vs TRIZ 0.526 (SD 0.206), t=-4.892, p=0.001. Second index 0.144 vs 0.230, p=0.009. Second-half process index difference not significant, t(9)=-0.195, p>0.05.
limits: Preliminary. Tasks differed between conditions. No outcome quality measured. Small N.
agent_relevance: TRIZ works partly by forcing problem restatement before solutions. That is S1/S2 work, matching O4 (restate) rather than any special principle content.

source: Duran-Novoa and Torres-Benoni (2024) Unveiling the impact of design methods on problem-solving performance in undergraduate STEM education, JOTSE 14(3)
finding: 144 students in 72 pairs, 3 Chilean universities, 4 conditions: contradiction matrix (MaTriz), SCAMPER, KJ-technique, no-method control. Two problems (cutting board, peanut shelling). Scored on novelty, variety, quality by experts. MaTriz scored best everywhere; control worst. The best method was the least preferred.
numbers: Problem 1 means (novelty/variety/quality, 0-4): Control 0.7/1.1/1.6; KJ 0.9/2.2/3.1; SCAMPER 1.8/2.5/3.3; MaTriz 2.3/3.1/3.5. Overall, SCAMPER 89%, KJ 73%, control 54% of MaTriz's score. Principle-based methods 54% higher on problem 1. Harder problem: novelty +15%, variety +11%, quality -34%. SCAMPER chosen by 52 teams when free, vs 56 for MaTriz and KJ combined.
limits: Control came from one university only. Institutions differed in year level. Assigned and chosen conditions unbalanced. Problem difficulty assumed by authors. Expert-rated scores. Statistical tables not read in full.
agent_relevance: Strongest recent controlled support for the matrix versus no method. The edge over SCAMPER is small (11%). Teams started later with MaTriz; the wait-and-study phase may be the active ingredient.

source: Duran-Novoa and Torres-Benoni (2024) JOTSE - discussion of prior studies
finding: Authors list earlier work that agrees: Gero et al. 2013 and Duran-Novoa et al. 2019 found structured methods beat intuitive ones. Chulvi et al. 2013 found brainstorming better, but only one team used it.
numbers: No new numbers. One-team brainstorming arm in Chulvi et al. 2013.
limits: Summaries of papers I did not open. Chulvi et al. and Duran-Novoa 2019 should be opened in a later pass.
agent_relevance: Evidence is mostly student pairs and small N. Do not assume transfer to a language model.

source: Vargas-Hernandez et al. (2012) ASEE paper - literature section
finding: Cites earlier work: a 153-senior study (95% mechanical) with patent analogies raised novelty but cut idea count; a study combining brainstorming with TRIZ on air velocity control raised novelty, variety and quality.
numbers: 153 seniors; energy-harvesting device task (from the paper's description).
limits: Second-hand summaries inside the paper. The 153-student study is the Linsey/Murphy style analogy experiment and is about patent analogies, not TRIZ itself.
agent_relevance: The 'more novel, fewer ideas' tradeoff appears across stimulus-based methods, not only TRIZ. Worth testing in the agent as a general cost.

source: Ogot and Okudan (2006) - course experience
finding: Students found the matrix tedious and confusing: many tables, number lookup, too few examples. Teams drifted from the principles without supervision. In-class guided practice fixed this.
numbers: 14 sections of 32 students in the course; 4 per team; TRIZ taught in 2 sections (64 students).
limits: Instructor observations and end-of-term evaluations, not coded data.
agent_relevance: Lookup burden is a model-friendly job (code does the lookup). Drift from the chosen principle needs a code monitor, which fits the schema.

source: Hernandez et al. 2012 / Trapp 2024 / TRIZBench 2026 - cross-reading
finding: Across LLM studies, all use small case sets (10, 10, 1, 1) or label sets from textbooks and patents. None compares typed TRIZ reframes against free reframing at equal tokens. TRIZBench itself says prior TRIZ-LLM work is small-scale and case-study based.
numbers: Case counts: AutoTRIZ 10; TRIZ-GPT 37+10; TRIZ Agents 1; Text-to-CAD 1; Trapp 100 patents; TRIZBench 1,354 cases.
limits: My synthesis across the papers I opened; not a systematic review. Paper list came from a single arXiv listing of 8 results.
agent_relevance: For O4/O8 the honest status is [S]/[D]: plausible, anecdotal, untested at equal compute. A matched-token ablation in our harness would be the first real evidence.

source: Linsey et al.-type 153-student patent-analogy study (cited in search result)
finding: Reported through the ASEE paper only; original not opened.
numbers: 153 seniors reported by a search snippet.
limits: Not read.
agent_relevance: Placeholder; open original in a follow-up.
